scope_notes: Covers kickboxing stance/guard, roundhouse kick (body/head), low kick to the thigh, teep (push kick), shin check, and punch-kick combination flow. Punch mechanics reuse the boxing KB (USA Boxing sources). Knees/elbows/clinch not yet covered.
source_gap_notes: Only ~9 strong sources: roundhouse-kick biomechanics and kickboxing match analysis are well studied, but teep and shin-check cues rely on tier-2/3 coaching resources (Evolve University; Muay Thai Bible). WAKO coaching manuals are not publicly available (rules only).

sources.name: Gavagan CJ, Sayers MGL - Biomechanical analysis of the roundhouse kick of expert practitioners: Muay Thai vs Karate vs Taekwondo (PLOS One 2017)
sources.credibility: 3D motion capture of experts; Muay Thai kick characterized by rapid forward pelvic axial rotation, hip abduction/flexion, knee extension and forward COM movement.

sources.name: Kinematic Comparison of the Roundhouse Kick (J Strength Cond Res 2021)
sources.credibility: NSCA journal; Muay Thai showed greater peak hip angular velocity with a shorter body-to-target distance than Taekwondo/Karate.

sources.name: Lower limb kinematics during roundhouse kick among novices in Muay Thai (J Fundamental and Applied Sciences)
sources.credibility: Novice roundhouse kinematics - useful for typical beginner patterns.
sources.usage_note: Background: describes novice kicking patterns; not cited for a specific item.

sources.name: Ouergui I et al. - Technical and tactical analysis of high level kickboxing matches (Int J Performance Analysis in Sport 2013)
sources.credibility: 45 elite matches: straight punches, roundhouse kicks, blocks/parries and foot defense most frequent; winners used more hooks, foot defense, clinches and combinations.

sources.name: Kickboxing review: anthropometric, psychophysiological and activity profiles and injury epidemiology (Biology of Sport, PMC)
sources.credibility: Review of kickboxing demands (aerobic/anaerobic power, limb power, activity:rest ratios) and injuries.

sources.name: Time-Motion Analysis of Elite Male Kickboxing Competition (J Strength Cond Res)
sources.credibility: Activity/rest structure of elite bouts - informs drill work:rest design.

sources.name: WAKO Low Kick Rules v17.4 (WAKO USA)
sources.credibility: World Association of Kickboxing Organizations rules: legal targets (e.g., low kicks to the thigh) and scoring.

sources.name: Evolve University - 4 Tips For A Powerful Muay Thai Roundhouse Kick
sources.credibility: Evolve MMA (Singapore) Muay Thai world-champion instructors; step-and-pivot, arm action, drive-through cues.

sources.name: Evolve University - Muay Thai Fundamentals course
sources.credibility: Course outline taught by Muay Thai world champions: stance, footwork, kicks, punches, knees, elbows, defense.

sources.name: Muay Thai Bible - Shin Block / Check and Teep as Defense technique guides
sources.credibility: Community technique encyclopedia; used ONLY for teep/check cues where tier-1 sources were not found. Tier 3.

sources.name: USA Boxing - The Sweet Science 101
sources.credibility: Used for punch mechanics inside kickboxing combinations (see boxing KB).

skills.name: Kickboxing stance and guard
skills.recommended_camera: Front and side views, full body.

checkpoints.description: Balanced base: one foot ahead of the other, hips more square to the opponent than a boxing stance, light on the feet so either leg can kick or check.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hip line ~20-45 deg to opponent (more square than boxing); weight roughly centered between feet

checkpoints.description: Hands high protecting the head; elbows in to cover the body.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: both wrists at or above chin height; elbows within ~1 fist of the torso

faults.name: Too bladed / heavy on the lead leg
faults.video_signs: Side-on boxing stance with weight forward; lead thigh exposed to low kicks and slow to check.
faults.correction_cue: 'Square up a little, weight centered - ready to lift either leg.'
faults.why_it_matters: A more square, centered stance allows quick checks and kicks off both legs.

pro_tips.tip: A good base is the foundation for kick power - without it you feel unstable as weight shifts for the kick and are easier to sweep.
Elite kickboxing bouts run at roughly a 1:1 activity-to-rest ratio (national/amateur bouts ~1:2 to 1:5) - match pad-round work:rest to the athlete's competition level.

skills.name: Roundhouse kick (body/head)
skills.recommended_camera: Front view (as the opponent) and side view; 120-240 fps; also top-down if possible to measure pelvis rotation.

checkpoints.description: Step the lead (support) foot out at ~45 degrees before kicking, toward the outside of the opponent.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: support foot displaced laterally and turned out ~45 deg from the stance position before the kick

checkpoints.description: Rise onto the ball of the support foot and pivot it so the heel turns toward the target.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: support heel lifts and rotates; support foot rotation ~90-180 deg from stance by impact

checkpoints.description: Rapid forward pelvic axial rotation drives the kick (pelvis turns over), with hip abduction/flexion followed by knee extension.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: pelvis rotation (hip line) ~80-180 deg through the kick; peak pelvis rotation velocity precedes peak knee extension velocity

checkpoints.description: Same-side arm swings down/back toward the kick for counterbalance while the opposite hand stays at the face.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: non-kicking-side wrist within ~1 fist of the face during the kick

checkpoints.description: Strike with the shin and drive through the target rather than stopping at it; return to a stable stance.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: kicking leg continues past the target line after contact; feet return to stance width

faults.name: Flat, planted support foot (no pivot)
faults.video_signs: Support heel stays on the floor and toes point at the opponent; kick stops short, knee feels torqued.
faults.correction_cue: 'Up on the ball of the foot and turn the heel to the target.'
faults.why_it_matters: Without the pivot the hips can't turn over - less power and more knee strain.

faults.name: No hip turnover (snapping from the knee)
faults.video_signs: Kick is thrown like a flick from the knee with the hips square; little follow-through.
faults.correction_cue: 'Turn the hips over - kick through, like swinging a bat.'
faults.why_it_matters: Pelvic rotation is the main power contributor in the Muay Thai kick.

faults.name: Arm thrown backward / guard dropped
faults.video_signs: Kicking-side arm flings behind the body; opposite hand drops from the face.
faults.correction_cue: 'Reach toward the kick; other glove on your cheek.'
faults.why_it_matters: A rear-flung arm pulls the shoulder out of alignment and exposes the head to counters.

faults.name: Kicking from too far away / reaching
faults.video_signs: Athlete leans back and reaches with the foot instead of the shin.
faults.correction_cue: 'Step in - land the shin, not the foot.'
faults.why_it_matters: Muay Thai kicks are thrown at a shorter distance to land the shin with full hip rotation.

drills.name: Step-and-pivot wall drill
drills.setup: Stand facing a wall or post, hands on it lightly for balance.
steps: Step the support foot out 45 deg.
Rise onto the ball and pivot the heel toward the target while turning the hips over.
Swing the kicking leg slowly to target height and return.
Then repeat without the wall, adding the arm swing and guard.
drills.dosage: 3 sets x 10 slow reps each side
drills.fixes: Flat support foot; arm thrown backward
drills.why: Removing the impact and speed lets the athlete groove the step-pivot-hip sequence that Evolve's coaches identify as essential for power.

drills.name: Heavy-bag kick-through drill
drills.setup: Heavy bag; mark a target line on the bag at body or thigh height.
steps: Throw single roundhouse kicks, landing with the lower shin.
Kick 'through' the bag - imagine the target is behind it.
Return to stance and reset; then add a jab-cross before each kick.
drills.fixes: No hip turnover; kicking from too far
drills.why: Driving through a heavy target trains full pelvic rotation and correct striking distance under real impact.

pro_tips.tip: Muay Thai roundhouse experts generate the kick with rapid pelvis rotation and move their centre of mass forward into the target.
Muay Thai stylists showed greater peak hip angular velocity and a shorter body-to-target distance than Karate/Taekwondo stylists - close the range before kicking.
In elite kickboxing, straight punches and roundhouse kicks are the most frequently used techniques, and winners use more combinations - drill kicks at the end of punch combinations.

checkpoints.description: Same hip-turnover mechanics as the roundhouse but aimed down at the thigh (between hip and knee); strike with the shin.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: impact point above the opponent's knee and below the hip (WAKO low-kick legal target); kicking shin roughly horizontal-to-downward

checkpoints.description: Hands stay up during the kick; often set up behind punches.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: opposite wrist at face during kick

faults.name: Kicking with the foot/instep at close range
faults.video_signs: Contact made with the foot or ankle instead of the shin.
faults.why_it_matters: The foot is fragile and easily checked; the shin is the striking surface.

faults.name: Telegraphed low kick
faults.video_signs: Kick thrown alone from a static stance, with an obvious step.
faults.why_it_matters: Unset-up kicks are easily checked or countered.

drills.name: Jab-cross-low kick combination flow
drills.setup: Pad holder with Thai pads, or heavy bag.
steps: Jab, cross, then low kick with the side the cross loaded.
Return to stance with guard up.
Pad holder occasionally returns a jab to check the guard.
drills.dosage: 4 rounds x 2 min; work:rest matched to bout demands
drills.why: Punch-kick flows mirror the combination patterns used by winning elite kickboxers and make kicks harder to read.

pro_tips.tip: Check the legal target for your rule set: WAKO low-kick rules permit kicks to the thigh; full-contact rules do not.

checkpoints.description: Lift the knee first (chamber), then extend through the ball of the foot into the hips/abdomen; keep the hands high.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: knee rises to roughly hip height before extension; hip extension on impact

checkpoints.description: Retract immediately and return to stance.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: foot returns to stance position quickly (< ~0.5 s after impact)

faults.name: Leaning far back / pushing without chamber
faults.video_signs: Leg extends without knee lift; torso leans back heavily.
faults.correction_cue: 'Knee up first, then push through the target.'
faults.why_it_matters: Without a chamber the kick is weak and easily caught.

drills.name: Teep-on-entry pad drill
drills.setup: Pad holder with a belly pad/kick shield steps forward at random.
steps: Kicker in stance; holder steps in.
Kicker lifts the lead knee first, then teeps into the pad with the ball of the foot, hands high.
Retract immediately to stance; alternate lead and rear teeps.
drills.why: Timing the teep to the holder's entry rehearses its main job - stopping forward pressure - while the chamber cue keeps it strong.

pro_tips.tip: Use the teep to stop forward pressure and measure range (tier-3 source; verify with your coach's system).

checkpoints.description: Read the hip/shoulder turn, lift the targeted leg's knee and turn the shin outward so the shin meets the kick; hands stay at the chin.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: checking knee lifts to ~hip height and angles outward; wrists remain at face

checkpoints.description: Supporting leg stays slightly bent; reset to stance immediately.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: support knee angle < ~170 deg during the check

faults.name: Late lift / dropped guard / straight support leg
faults.video_signs: Knee lifts after the kick lands; hands drop; support leg locked.
faults.correction_cue: 'Lift early, hands home, soft support knee.'
faults.why_it_matters: Late checks take the full kick; dropped hands invite punches.

drills.name: Reaction check drill
drills.setup: Partner with shin guards throws light low kicks at random intervals.
steps: On the partner's hip turn, lift and check.
Return a cross or low kick immediately after the check.
drills.fixes: Late check; heavy lead leg; dropped guard
drills.why: Random, light kicks train reading the hip turn and reacting early, then link the check to a counter.

pro_tips.tip: Foot defense (checks/evasions) was more frequent among winners in elite kickboxing matches.
